Per-share residual-income intrinsic-value measure based on current book value and expected future abnormal earnings. EPS forecasts for years +1 and +2 are IBES means; for fewer than 5% of firm-years, IBES forecasts are available through year +5, and otherwise the mean long-term growth forecast g is applied recursively to the preceding mean forecast for years +3 to +5. Future book value follows the ex-ante clean-surplus relation: prior book value plus forecast EPS minus forecast dividends. Current indicated annual dividends divided by year+1 EPS forecast define the payout ratio; it is held constant for future dividends and winsorized to lie between 10% and 50%. Indicated annual dividends are four times the latest quarter’s declared dividends, and EPS1 is used as deflator. The discount rate k_t is the 10-year Treasury yield on April 1 of t+1 plus beta times a 5% equity risk premium; beta is the same-year median beta of firms in the same beta decile. The underlying beta estimator is not stated. P1 assumes abnormal earnings remain constant after year +5. The Appendix A terminal term is transcribed as printed with unbound s; its horizon/exponent meaning is unresolved.. Preserve Appendix A’s item codes and product definitions; the live route confirms only field presence and requires independent semantic/date linkage. The source’s printed P1 terminal term and P3 ROE horizon conflict with its prose; do not replace them with a silent correction.
